question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of an Inverse Function From a Graph
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13979325/assets/ba762e13c4015b43b99f9038ee63a247584345cd535e12b80c1f3b0d9e50e70b.png)

The figure above shows the graph of a piecewise linear function $y=f(x).$ The point $A$ has coordinates $(1,0)$ and lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $(0,1)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x),$ what is $({f}^{-1})^{′}(0)?$
question.worked_solution:
Since $(0,1)$ lies on ${f}^{-1},$ we have ${f}^{-1}(0)=1.$ 
The slope of the tangent to $f(x)$ for $x\in [0,2]$ is $-2$, hence, ${f}^{′}(1)=-2.$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse function is 

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Evaluating at $x=0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(0) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(0))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{-2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of an Inverse Function
question.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=\frac{3+4x}{2-3x}$ and the point $P(1,-7)$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$ determine the slope of $y={f}^{-1}(x)$ at the point $(-7,1).$
question.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(1,-7).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{3+4x}{2-3x} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{17}{(2-3x)^{2}} \\ {f}^{′}(1) & =17\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(1,-7)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(-7,1)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(-7) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(-7))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{17}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Derivative of an Inverse Function Using a Table
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse is

$$
({g}^{-1})^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{{g}^{′}({g}^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Substituting $x=-2,$ we have

$$
({g}^{-1})^{′}(-2)=\frac{1}{{g}^{′}({g}^{-1}(-2))}.
$$

From the table, we obtain ${g}^{-1}(-2)=1$ and ${g}^{′}(1)=8.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}({g}^{-1})^{′}(-2) & =\frac{1}{{g}^{′}({g}^{-1}(-2))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{g}^{′}(1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Finding a Derivative Using Properties of Inverse Functions
question.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=\sqrt{2x-1}.$ Given that $y=f(x)$ is invertible throughout its domain, determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(3).$
question.worked_solution:
To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(3),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(3)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(3))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(3).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(3)=x.$ For $x>\frac{1}{2}$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(3) & =x \\ f(x) & =3 \\ \sqrt{2x-1} & =3 \\ 2x-1 & =9 \\ 2x & =10 \\ x & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate ${f}^{′}(5),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\sqrt{2x-1} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2x-1}} \\ {f}^{′}(5) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\cdot 5-1}} \\ {f}^{′}(5) & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(3) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(3))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(5)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
